fields.name: initial_sigma

fields.help: Starting volatility: how quickly a team’s underlying strength may change. Typical starting value: 0.06.

fields.name: tau
fields.title: Tau
fields.help: Limits how rapidly volatility can change. Larger tau allows more adaptation; it is not a rolling window.

fields.name: tolerance

ratings.GlickoTransition.title: GlickoTransition
ratings.GlickoTransition.description: Optional seasonal RD inflation and movement shrinkage; sigma unchanged.

fields.name: phi_scale
fields.title: Phi scale

fields.name: movement_phi_scale

fields.name: shrinkage

fields.help: Amount of past data used for fitting, measured in the selected unit. Example: 2 seasons.

fields.name: test_size

fields.name: step

fields.name: window

fields.help: Expanding retains all eligible earlier training blocks; sliding retains a fixed train_size window as the test window moves forward.

fields.help: Training, test and step use this unit. Seasons combines the same season across leagues into one fold. League-seasons creates separate folds and fitted models per league. Example: four seasons with train 2/test 1 gives two pooled folds, or two folds per league. Gap unit can be set independently.

fields.name: gap
fields.title: Gap

fields.name: gap_time

fields.name: calendar_by

fields.help: Advanced override for independent calendars. Seasons pools leagues by default; League-seasons and Rounds separate competitions. An enabled empty selection pools calendars.

fields.name: block_by
fields.title: Block by
fields.help: Optional metadata identifiers that must stay together at split boundaries.

fields.name: score_start
fields.title: Score start

fields.name: score_rounds

fields.help: Inclusive round-number range [first, last] to score in each test season. Either bound may be left empty. Disabled scores all eligible test rounds.

fields.name: allow_partial_test
fields.title: Allow partial test
fields.help: Include a final test window even if fewer than test_size units remain.

fields.name: gap_unit
fields.title: Gap unit
fields.help: Disabled uses the window unit. Choose Rounds with season windows to skip opening test rounds: gap 10 starts testing at round 11 in each league and keeps the season end. Kickoffs counts simultaneous kickoff batches. Choose the same or a finer unit than the window.

fields.name: tol
fields.title: Tol
fields.help: The precision of the solution (`coef_`) is determined by `tol` which specifies the convergence criterion of the underlying solver. `tol` is set as `atol` and `btol` of :func:`scipy.sparse.linalg.lsqr` when fitting on sparse training data. `tol` is set as `cond` of :func:`scipy.linalg.lstsq` when fitting on dense training data.

fields.name: n_jobs
fields.title: N jobs
fields.help: The number of jobs to use for the computation. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>` for more details.

fields.name: positive
fields.title: Positive
fields.help: When set to ``True``, forces the coefficients to be positive. This option is only supported for dense arrays.

sklearn.linear_model.PoissonRegressor.description: Generalized Linear Model with a Poisson distribution.

fields.name: fit_intercept
fields.title: Fit intercept
fields.help: Specifies if a constant (a.k.a. bias or intercept) should be added to the linear predictor (`X @ coef + intercept`).

fields.name: solver

fields.help: Algorithm to use in the optimization problem:

fields.name: max_iter
fields.title: Max iter
fields.help: The maximal number of iterations for the solver. Values must be in the range `[1, inf)`.

fields.name: tol
fields.title: Tol
fields.help: Stopping criterion. For the lbfgs solver, the iteration will stop when ``max{|g_j|, j = 1, ..., d} <= tol`` where ``g_j`` is the j-th component of the gradient (derivative) of the objective function. Values must be in the range `(0.0, inf)`.

fields.name: warm_start
fields.title: Warm start
fields.help: If set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to ``fit`` as initialization for ``coef_`` and ``intercept_`` .

fields.name: verbose
fields.title: Verbose
fields.help: For the lbfgs solver set verbose to any positive number for verbosity. Values must be in the range `[0, inf)`.

fields.name: penalty
fields.title: Penalty

fields.name: C
fields.title: C
fields.help: Inverse of regularization strength; must be a positive float. Like in support vector machines, smaller values specify stronger regularization. `C=np.inf` results in unpenalized logistic regression. For a visual example on the effect of tuning the `C` parameter with an L1 penalty, see: :ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_logistic_path.py`.

fields.name: l1_ratio

fields.help: The Elastic-Net mixing parameter, with `0 <= l1_ratio <= 1`. Setting `l1_ratio=1` gives a pure L1-penalty, setting `l1_ratio=0` a pure L2-penalty. Any value between 0 and 1 gives an Elastic-Net penalty of the form `l1_ratio * L1 + (1 - l1_ratio) * L2`.

fields.name: dual
fields.title: Dual
fields.help: Dual (constrained) or primal (regularized, see also :ref:`this equation <regularized-logistic-loss>`) formulation. Dual formulation is only implemented for l2 penalty with liblinear solver. Prefer `dual=False` when n_samples > n_features.

fields.name: tol

fields.name: fit_intercept

fields.name: intercept_scaling

The intercept becomes ``intercept_scaling * synthetic_feature_weight``.

fields.name: class_weight
fields.title: Class weight

fields.name: random_state

fields.name: n_jobs

fields.title: Loss
fields.help: The loss function to be used. The possible values are 'squared_error', 'huber', 'epsilon_insensitive', or 'squared_epsilon_insensitive'

fields.name: penalty
fields.title: Penalty
fields.help: The penalty (aka regularization term) to be used. Defaults to 'l2' which is the standard regularizer for linear SVM models. 'l1' and 'elasticnet' might bring sparsity to the model (feature selection) not achievable with 'l2'. No penalty is added when set to `None`.

fields.name: alpha
fields.title: Alpha
fields.help: Constant that multiplies the regularization term. The higher the value, the stronger the regularization. Also used to compute the learning rate when `learning_rate` is set to 'optimal'. Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.

fields.name: l1_ratio
fields.title: L1 ratio
fields.help: The Elastic Net mixing parameter, with 0 <= l1_ratio <= 1. l1_ratio=0 corresponds to L2 penalty, l1_ratio=1 to L1. Only used if `penalty` is 'elasticnet'. Values must be in the range `[0.0, 1.0]` or can be `None` if `penalty` is not `elasticnet`.

fields.name: fit_intercept

fields.help: Whether the intercept should be estimated or not. If False, the data is assumed to be already centered.

fields.name: max_iter

fields.help: The maximum number of passes over the training data (aka epochs). It only impacts the behavior in the ``fit`` method, and not the :meth:`partial_fit` method. Values must be in the range `[1, inf)`.

fields.name: tol
fields.title: Tol
fields.help: The stopping criterion. If it is not None, training will stop when (loss > best_loss - tol) for ``n_iter_no_change`` consecutive epochs. Convergence is checked against the training loss or the validation loss depending on the `early_stopping` parameter. Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.

fields.name: shuffle
fields.title: Shuffle
fields.help: Whether or not the training data should be shuffled after each epoch.

fields.name: verbose
fields.title: Verbose
fields.help: The verbosity level. Values must be in the range `[0, inf)`.

fields.name: epsilon
fields.title: Epsilon
fields.help: Epsilon in the epsilon-insensitive loss functions; only if `loss` is 'huber', 'epsilon_insensitive', or 'squared_epsilon_insensitive'. For 'huber', determines the threshold at which it becomes less important to get the prediction exactly right. For epsilon-insensitive, any differences between the current prediction and the correct label are ignored if they are less than this threshold. Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.

fields.name: random_state
fields.title: Random state
fields.help: Used for shuffling the data, when ``shuffle`` is set to ``True``. Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.

fields.name: learning_rate
fields.title: Learning rate
fields.help: The learning rate schedule:

fields.name: eta0
fields.title: Eta0
fields.help: The initial learning rate for the 'constant', 'invscaling' or 'adaptive' schedules. The default value is 0.01. Values must be in the range `(0.0, inf)`.

fields.name: power_t
fields.title: Power t
fields.help: The exponent for inverse scaling learning rate. Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.

fields.name: early_stopping
fields.title: Early stopping
fields.help: Whether to use early stopping to terminate training when validation score is not improving. If set to True, it will automatically set aside a fraction of training data as validation and terminate training when validation score returned by the `score` method is not improving by at least `tol` for `n_iter_no_change` consecutive epochs.

fields.name: validation_fraction
fields.title: Validation fraction
fields.help: The proportion of training data to set aside as validation set for early stopping. Must be between 0 and 1. Only used if `early_stopping` is True. Values must be in the range `(0.0, 1.0)`.

fields.name: n_iter_no_change
fields.title: N iter no change
fields.help: Number of iterations with no improvement to wait before stopping fitting. Convergence is checked against the training loss or the validation loss depending on the `early_stopping` parameter. Integer values must be in the range `[1, max_iter)`.

fields.name: warm_start
fields.title: Warm start
fields.help: When set to True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit as initialization, otherwise, just erase the previous solution. See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.

fields.name: average
fields.title: Average
fields.help: When set to True, computes the averaged SGD weights across all updates and stores the result in the ``coef_`` attribute. If set to an int greater than 1, averaging will begin once the total number of samples seen reaches `average`. So ``average=10`` will begin averaging after seeing 10 samples.

fields.name: max_depth

fields.name: min_samples_split
fields.title: Min samples split

fields.name: min_samples_leaf

fields.help: The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node. A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model, especially in regression.

fields.name: min_weight_fraction_leaf
fields.title: Min weight fraction leaf
fields.help: The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.

fields.name: max_features

fields.name: max_leaf_nodes

fields.help: Grow trees with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion. Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity. If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.

fields.name: min_impurity_decrease
fields.title: Min impurity decrease
fields.help: A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity greater than or equal to this value.

fields.name: bootstrap

fields.name: oob_score

fields.help: If 'auto', early stopping is enabled if the sample size is larger than 10000 or if `X_val` and `y_val` are passed to `fit`. If True, early stopping is enabled, otherwise early stopping is disabled.

fields.name: scoring
fields.title: Scoring
fields.help: Scoring method to use for early stopping. Only used if `early_stopping` is enabled. Options:

fields.name: validation_fraction
fields.title: Validation fraction
fields.help: Proportion (or absolute size) of training data to set aside as validation data for early stopping. If None, early stopping is done on the training data. The value is ignored if either early stopping is not performed, e.g. `early_stopping=False`, or if `X_val` and `y_val` are passed to fit.

fields.name: n_iter_no_change
fields.title: N iter no change
fields.help: Used to determine when to "early stop". The fitting process is stopped when none of the last ``n_iter_no_change`` scores are better than the ``n_iter_no_change - 1`` -th-to-last one, up to some tolerance. Only used if early stopping is performed.

fields.name: tol
fields.title: Tol
fields.help: The absolute tolerance to use when comparing scores during early stopping. The higher the tolerance, the more likely we are to early stop: higher tolerance means that it will be harder for subsequent iterations to be considered an improvement upon the reference score.

fields.name: verbose
fields.title: Verbose
fields.help: The verbosity level. If not zero, print some information about the fitting process. ``1`` prints only summary info, ``2`` prints info per iteration.

fields.name: random_state
fields.title: Random state
fields.help: Pseudo-random number generator to control the subsampling in the binning process, and the train/validation data split if early stopping is enabled. Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.

fields.name: loss
fields.title: Loss
fields.help: The loss function to use in the boosting process.

fields.name: learning_rate
fields.title: Learning rate
fields.help: The learning rate, also known as *shrinkage*. This is used as a multiplicative factor for the leaves values. Use ``1`` for no shrinkage.

fields.name: max_iter
fields.title: Max iter
fields.help: The maximum number of iterations of the boosting process, i.e. the maximum number of trees for binary classification. For multiclass classification, `n_classes` trees per iteration are built.

fields.name: max_leaf_nodes
fields.title: Max leaf nodes
fields.help: The maximum number of leaves for each tree. Must be strictly greater than 1. If None, there is no maximum limit.

fields.name: max_depth
fields.title: Max depth
fields.help: The maximum depth of each tree. The depth of a tree is the number of edges to go from the root to the deepest leaf. Depth isn't constrained by default.

fields.name: min_samples_leaf
fields.title: Min samples leaf
fields.help: The minimum number of samples per leaf. For small datasets with less than a few hundred samples, it is recommended to lower this value since only very shallow trees would be built.

fields.name: l2_regularization
fields.title: L2 regularization
fields.help: The L2 regularization parameter penalizing leaves with small hessians. Use ``0`` for no regularization (default).

fields.name: max_features
fields.title: Max features
fields.help: Proportion of randomly chosen features in each and every node split. This is a form of regularization, smaller values make the trees weaker learners and might prevent overfitting. If interaction constraints from `interaction_cst` are present, only allowed features are taken into account for the subsampling.

fields.name: max_bins
fields.title: Max bins
fields.help: The maximum number of bins to use for non-missing values. Before training, each feature of the input array `X` is binned into integer-valued bins, which allows for a much faster training stage. Features with a small number of unique values may use less than ``max_bins`` bins. In addition to the ``max_bins`` bins, one more bin is always reserved for missing values. Must be no larger than 255.

fields.name: output_distribution

fields.name: sparse_output

fields.name: dtype

If `None`, there is no limit to the number of output features.

fields.name: feature_name_combiner

fields.help: If a single int is given, it specifies the maximal degree of the polynomial features. If a tuple `(min_degree, max_degree)` is passed, then `min_degree` is the minimum and `max_degree` is the maximum polynomial degree of the generated features. Note that `min_degree=0` and `min_degree=1` are equivalent as outputting the degree zero term is determined by `include_bias`.

fields.name: interaction_only
fields.title: Interaction only
fields.help: If `True`, only interaction features are produced: features that are products of at most `degree` *distinct* input features, i.e. terms with power of 2 or higher of the same input feature are excluded:

training.NegativeBinomialRegressor.title: Negative Binomial regression
training.NegativeBinomialRegressor.description: Count regression with a log link and optional Ridge, Lasso or Elastic Net penalties. Choose mean or mode predictions; variance is mean + dispersion × mean². Keep target labels unscaled; standardize inputs when penalizing coefficients.

fields.name: dispersion
fields.title: Dispersion
fields.help: NB2 variance = mean + dispersion × mean². Positive and fixed during fitting; tune it in Model selection. For mean 10, dispersion 0.2 gives variance 30. This is not a regularization penalty.

fields.name: fit_intercept
fields.title: Fit intercept
fields.help: Learn the baseline log mean. Usually enabled; disabling assumes an expected count of 1 when all transformed inputs are zero.

fields.name: max_iter
fields.title: Max iter
fields.help: Maximum iterations used to fit coefficients. Increase if fitting reports that convergence was not reached.

fields.name: tol
fields.title: Tol
fields.help: Tolerance for convergence of the fitting algorithm. Smaller values require a more precise fit.

fields.name: penalty
fields.title: Penalty
fields.help: None preserves ordinary NB regression. Ridge shrinks coefficients; Lasso can set them to zero; Elastic Net combines both. The intercept is never penalized. Standardize inputs before using a penalty.

fields.name: alpha
fields.title: Penalty strength
fields.help: Penalty strength, separate from Dispersion. Zero disables shrinkage. Try 0.001, 0.01, 0.1 and 1 in grid search. Larger values shrink fitted-feature coefficients more strongly.

fields.name: l1_ratio
fields.title: L1 ratio
fields.help: Elastic Net mixture: 0 is pure Ridge, 1 is pure Lasso, and 0.5 mixes both equally. Used only with Elastic Net.

fields.name: prediction
fields.title: Predict using
fields.help: Mean returns the expected count. Mode returns the most probable integer count (upper mode for ties). With dispersion 1 or greater, the mode is always zero. This changes the prediction summary, not the fitting objective, and does not guarantee wider predictions.

targets.StandardScaler.title: Standard target scaler
targets.StandardScaler.description: Center labels by their mean and scale by their standard deviation. Learns from fitting rows only; predictions are automatically restored to original units.

fields.name: copy
fields.title: Copy
fields.help: Keep input arrays unchanged when possible. Disable to allow in-place work; the target adapter still isolates the original labels.

fields.name: with_mean
fields.title: With mean
fields.help: Subtract the mean learned from fitting rows. Disable to preserve the original zero point.

fields.name: with_std
fields.title: With std
fields.help: Divide by the standard deviation learned from fitting rows.

targets.MinMaxScaler.title: Min-max target scaler
targets.MinMaxScaler.description: Map the fitting label range to a chosen interval, usually 0 to 1. Learns from fitting rows only; predictions are automatically restored to original units.

fields.name: feature_range
fields.title: Feature range
fields.help: Output interval, for example 0 to 1.

fields.name: copy
fields.title: Copy
fields.help: Keep input arrays unchanged when possible. Disable to allow in-place work; the target adapter still isolates the original labels.

fields.name: clip
fields.title: Clip
fields.help: Clip transformed validation or future observations to the chosen interval. This loses information outside the fitting range; inverse transformation cannot undo clipping.

targets.MaxAbsScaler.title: Max-absolute target scaler
targets.MaxAbsScaler.description: Divide labels by their largest absolute fitting value without centering. Learns from fitting rows only; predictions are automatically restored to original units.

fields.name: copy
fields.title: Copy
fields.help: Keep input arrays unchanged when possible. Disable to allow in-place work; the target adapter still isolates the original labels.

fields.name: clip
fields.title: Clip
fields.help: Clip for Max-absolute target scaler. Default: False.

targets.RobustScaler.title: Robust target scaler
targets.RobustScaler.description: Center labels by their median and scale by a chosen percentile range. Learns from fitting rows only; predictions are automatically restored to original units.

fields.name: with_centering
fields.title: With centering
fields.help: Subtract the median learned from fitting rows.

fields.name: with_scaling
fields.title: With scaling
fields.help: Divide by the spread between the selected fitting percentiles.

fields.name: quantile_range
fields.title: Quantile range
fields.help: Percentiles defining the robust scale; 25 and 75 use the interquartile range.

fields.name: copy
fields.title: Copy
fields.help: Keep input arrays unchanged when possible. Disable to allow in-place work; the target adapter still isolates the original labels.

fields.name: unit_variance
fields.title: Unit variance
fields.help: Adjust the percentile-based scale so a normal distribution would have variance one.

targets.QuantileTransformer.title: Quantile target transformer
targets.QuantileTransformer.description: Map label ranks to a uniform or normal distribution. Inverse predictions stay within the fitted quantile range. Learns from fitting rows only; predictions are automatically restored to original units.

fields.name: n_quantiles
fields.title: N quantiles
fields.help: Number of empirical quantile landmarks. Uses at most the number of fitting rows; 1000 is the usual starting point.

fields.name: output_distribution
fields.title: Output distribution
fields.help: Uniform maps ranks to 0–1; normal maps them to a bell-shaped distribution. This transforms values; it does not enable quantile regression.

fields.name: ignore_implicit_zeros
fields.title: Ignore implicit zeros
fields.help: For sparse input matrices only: exclude unstored zeros when estimating quantiles. Ordinary dense labels are unaffected.

fields.name: subsample
fields.title: Subsample
fields.help: Maximum fitting samples used to estimate quantiles. None uses every fitting row. If set, keep it at least as large as Quantile landmarks.

fields.name: random_state
fields.title: Random state
fields.help: Seed for reproducible subsampling. Set a number such as 0 to repeat the same fit sampling.

fields.name: copy
fields.title: Copy
fields.help: Keep input arrays unchanged when possible. Disable to allow in-place work; the target adapter still isolates the original labels.

targets.PowerTransformer.title: Power target transformer
targets.PowerTransformer.description: Reduce skew with Yeo-Johnson or Box-Cox. Box-Cox requires strictly positive labels. Learns from fitting rows only; predictions are automatically restored to original units.

fields.name: method
fields.title: Method
fields.help: Yeo-Johnson accepts zero and negative values. Box-Cox requires strictly positive values, so it cannot directly transform zero-corner labels.

fields.name: standardize
fields.title: Standardize
fields.help: After the power transform, also center to mean zero and scale to unit variance using fitting rows.

fields.name: copy
fields.title: Copy
fields.help: Keep input arrays unchanged when possible. Disable to allow in-place work; the target adapter still isolates the original labels.

fields.help: All available leagues are selected by default. Untick any league to exclude it.

fields.name: tables
fields.title: Tables
fields.help: Select prediction-relevant source tables. Matches identify fixtures; statistics supplies numeric observations; pregame supplies standings.

fields.name: record_dir
fields.title: Record dir
fields.help: Optional directory for loader resolution records. Disabled uses the loader default.

fields.name: verify_hashes
fields.title: Verify hashes
fields.help: Verify hashes for data. Default: False.

fields.name: include_awarded
fields.title: Include awarded
fields.help: Include administratively awarded matches. Disabled excludes them from training and histories.

stat_selection.title: stat_selection
stat_selection.description: Select the union of bundles and explicit (period, group_name, key) triples.

fields.name: bundles
fields.title: Bundles
fields.help: Convenience groups of statistics. Combine bundles with individually selected extra statistics.

fields.name: stats
fields.title: Stats
fields.help: Add specific statistics to the selected bundles.

fields.name: categories
fields.title: Categories
fields.help: Optional attack/defense category definitions used when expanding statistic bundles.

history.title: history
history.description: Return a DataFrame with two rows per match, ordered by UTC kickoff.

fields.name: stat_fields
fields.title: Stat fields
fields.help: Numeric statistic fields retained in team history. Value is the ordinary count or percentage; total is an optional denominator.

feature_options.title: feature_options
feature_options.description: Evaluate a mapping of output names to expressions; preserve row/index order.

fields.name: group_by
fields.title: Group by
fields.help: Rows with the same selected metadata identifiers stay together.

fields.name: cutoffs
fields.title: Cutoffs
fields.help: Optional information cutoff aligned with each row. The hours-before-kickoff control is the simpler choice.

fields.name: available_at
fields.title: Available at
fields.help: Optional result-availability timestamps. Disabled uses the documented retrospective finished-match assumption.

fields.name: team_counts
fields.title: Team counts
fields.help: Optional count Series indexed by competition_id and season_id for normalizing standings. Disabled counts distinct teams and opponents in the loaded history before fold filtering; a partial league sample may need full-population counts supplied here.

fields.name: ratings
fields.title: Ratings
fields.help: Named rating states available to Rating features. Configure these in Named rating states.

fields.name: team_seasons
fields.title: Team seasons
fields.help: Optional table keyed by competition_id, season_id and team_id, with movement and optional previous-league/season IDs. Disabled recognizes retained teams from loaded history; a new appearance alone does not establish promotion or relegation.

fields.name: season_starts
fields.title: Season starts
fields.help: Optional UTC season-entry boundaries used to freeze transition priors. Disabled uses the earliest prediction cutoff per league-season (first kickoff when no cutoff is supplied). Explicit boundaries cannot follow that first cutoff.

rating_options.title: rating_options
rating_options.description: Build saved-state data from the complete two-rows-per-match team history.

fields.name: stat
fields.title: Stat
fields.help: Leave disabled for win/draw/loss ratings. Enable to compare a statistic such as corner kicks instead.

fields.name: engine
fields.title: Engine
fields.help: Rating algorithm and initialization. The same settings apply to both teams before each update.

fields.name: higher_is_better
fields.title: Higher is better
fields.help: If enabled, the team with the larger statistic receives the win. Disable for quantities where smaller is better.

fields.name: scope
fields.title: Scope
fields.help: Keep rating streams separate by these identifiers. Competition gives each league its own ratings.

fields.name: available_at
fields.title: Available at
fields.help: Optional result-availability timestamps. Disabled uses the documented retrospective finished-match assumption.

fields.name: transition

fields.name: transition_context

assembly.title: assembly

fields.name: layout
